A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MPC-Flow research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison. The regularisation appendix moves from G to H, and retained material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original toy simulations, OrganCMNIST reconstruction experiments, CelebA restoration results and FLUX.2 style-transfer and colouration experiments, including quantitative results in Tables 2 and 3.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds baseline results, perceptual metrics, computational measurements, an HJB comparison and additional FLUX.2 and SD3.0 restoration examples.

M1.justification: Algorithm 3 is corrected by removing the assignment of the execution step δ to the entire remaining horizon and restoring λ before the terminal loss. These changes repair the written procedure to match the existing receding-horizon formulation; they do not establish a redesigned method or changed experimental implementation.

E1.justification: v2 adds FLUX.2 8× bicubic super-resolution and SD3.0 examples covering 12× bicubic and average-pooling super-resolution and deblurring. The latter use three samples from DIV2K, AFHQ and FFHQ, extending restoration coverage to natural scenes and animals under substantially stronger degradation scenarios. These are small demonstrations, not full evaluations of those datasets.

E2.justification: FlowChef and FlowDPS are added to the six-task CelebA comparison in Table 2, while every previous comparator remains. Both also participate in the new SD3.0 comparison. FlowChef was already evaluated with FLUX.2 in v1, but its CelebA participation is new.

E3.justification: v2 adds LPIPS to the CelebA evaluation, FLUX.2 memory/time measurements, and new protocols using 8× bicubic downsampling and SD3.0 with 12× downsampling. Appendix C adds a numerical HJB reference computed by a semi-Lagrangian scheme. One new setting remains inconsistent: Appendix G specifies Gaussian deblurring, whereas Figure F3 labels it motion deblurring.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds a substantive diagnostic of MPC-Δt's value-function approximation: Figure C3 compares it with an HJB solution, plots approximation error over time and compares controlled trajectories. This complements the retained MPC-RHC analysis. Figure 10 additionally examines the perception–measurement-consistency trade-off for FLUX.2 super-resolution.

E5.justification: Figure 10 newly specifies averaging over five random seeds for a single super-resolution image. This is a new experiment's run-count disclosure, not an increase from the three seeds used for colouration, which remains unchanged. No confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: All existing Table 2 scores and runtimes remain unchanged, but v2 adds FlowChef/FlowDPS results, CelebA LPIPS scores, HJB findings and latent-model restoration results. Table 4 newly reports MPC's 18.4 GB/101 s versus unconditional generation's 17.7 GB/53 s. New Table E1 also prints degraded super-resolution/inpainting SSIM as 0.182/0.197, conflicting with −0.182/−0.197 in both versions' Table 2.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 corrects Equation 15 from unsquared control norms to squared norms and identifies the squared L2 norm in the lower-semicontinuity argument. The formal assumptions, optimality theorems and other derivations are retained; the regularisation interpretation is relocated without substantive mathematical change.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the MPC formulation, its connection to idealised optimal control, restoration effectiveness and memory-efficient FLUX.2 guidance. The abstract changes 'theoretical guarantees' to 'theoretical analysis', but the same conditional theorems and principal scientific claims remain.

C2.justification: The conclusion explicitly separates continuous-time guarantees from Euler discretisation, inexact optimisation and the approximate value function. Appendix C explains early trajectory disagreement through value-approximation error. Section 4.2 also adds interpretations of FlowChef/FlowDPS performance involving regularisation, noise and null spaces. Existing initialisation and single-step limitations remain.

D1.justification: The code statement changes from future release to reported public availability. Appendix E newly states 100 time steps, adds FlowChef/FlowDPS hyperparameters, fills the previously missing OC-Flow nonlinear-deblurring settings and clarifies the MPC parameter tuples. These are documentation additions, not evidence that retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v2 acknowledges HardFlow as closely related concurrent work using receding-horizon MPC, adds DAPS to related work and cites mean-flow models as a possible future direction. Most other reference changes update publication metadata for already cited works, including FlowChef.

P1.justification: The core exposition and section sequence remain largely intact. Changes include local wording corrections, updated affiliation/publication information, additional experimental paragraphs, separate MPC-RHC/MPC-Δt discussion in Appendix C and a new SD3.0 appendix that shifts the regularisation section to H.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the displays with the HJB multipanel Figure C3, super-resolution Figure 10/F1, the SD3.0 montage F3 and its Figure 9 excerpt, computational Table 4 and LPIPS Table E1. Tables 2 and the hyperparameter table expand. Existing figures are largely retained; v1 Figure F1 becomes v2 Figure F2.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the comparisons more informative through additional baselines, perceptual metrics and measured resource costs, while correcting pseudocode and clarifying the practical limits of the theory. These are useful improvements over v1. Their overall impact is limited by the illustrative scale of the new latent-model studies and reporting inconsistencies, particularly the deblurring label and conflicting degraded-image SSIM signs.
